newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Banks lift Australian stocks to record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Banks lift Australian stocks to record close.

text.p: AORD 2501.70 +8.50 DJIA cl holiday
SPI Futures 2512 +20 US 30yr cl holiday
10yrbond futs 92.715 +0.005 Gold NY closed Lon fix 343.60
AUD 0.7668 (Mon 0.7643) CRB Index cl holiday
*Stocks crawl to record close, banks fuel market rise, rest narrowly mixed in modest trade. Volume 404.26 million, value A$928.39 million, 1,110 stocks traded, 337 steady, 369 up, 404 down.
A booming bank sector lifted an otherwise lacklustre Australian share market to a record close on Tuesday, the market crawling ahead despite a lack of inspiration from offshore markets.

By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 8.5 points higher at 2,501.7, surpassing the previous record close of 2,496.4, set on February 13. The all time high for the benchmark is 2,506.5, reached on February 14, 1997.
The March share price index futures contract was 20 points higher at 2,512, a 10.3 point premium to the underlying index.

National Australia Bank, convincingly hurdled the A$17.00 level to a record high A$17.15, and Commonwealth Bank of Australia, up 25 cents to A$13.62 after rebounding from going ex-dividend on Monday, led the in-demand sector to a 1.1 percent gain, outperforming the market benchmark's 0.34 percent gain.
Brokers said interest in the banks had boosted turnover figures, belying what was really a fairly slow day.
"It's been quite dull today with no real direction from overseas," said broker Dirk Van Der Struyf of Hartley Poynton.
"The market seems to be biding its time at the moment."
Shares in heavy engineering group Australian National Industries ended four cents higher at A$1.29 after a sharply higher half year net profit of A$16.33 million.

Gold major, Normandy Mining, added two cents to A$1.76 after posting a more than doubled first half net profit of A$51.6 million, while nickel miner QNI Ltd lost a cent to A$2.58 following a sharp fall in first half net profit to A$13.32 million. Aluminium producer, Capral Aluminium shares jumped 20 cents to A$4.30 after announcing a 25 cent per share special dividend. However, its full year net profit more than halved to A$29.42 million.

Golden Valley Mines shares dived to an early low of six cents before recovering some losses to end three cents lower at eight cents on heavy turnover of 27.6 million shares. This followed an announcement from Canadian-based miner Bre-X Mineral on the controversial Indonesian Busang gold deposit that failed to mention Golden Valley's joint venture partner.

Also at the smaller end, Grange Resources added nearly 20 percent to 15.5 cents on heavy turnover of 11.3 million shares after reporting encouraging results from its Mt Windsor copper/gold joint venture in Queensland.
Soft drink maker C-C Amatil dipped again, losing 75 cents to A$12.19 as traders continued to re-rate the stock after Friday's soft 1996 year net profit of A$142.1 million.

Shares in grocery wholesaler Davids Ltd headed lower, down six cents to A$1.60, on concerns about its ability to retain market share after Monday's announcement from grocery giant Woolworths that intended to expand its wholesale division.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about 11 to 10, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trade saw only moderate activity. Total options traded 37,325 (22,113)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 6,543 (5,459)

In other local markets, Australian bonds reined back their early price falls to show a modest rise by the close in response to the the Reserve Bank's positive inflation outlook. The RBA said in its quarterly Bulletin it expected a good performance on inflation in the near term and also saw underlying inflation remaining within its 2.0-3.0 percent target bank during 1998. By 5.45 p.m.(0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.26 percent.

The Australian dollar finished Tuesday on a firm note after an upbeat economic outlook from the Reserve Bank silenced all talk of a near term policy easing. Traders reported resistance at US$0.7675, where offshore offers were lurking, and good support at US$0.7635. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the unit had bobbed up to US$0.7665/70 from US$0.7639/44 late here Monday.
